pumac-2007-combinatorics-a-06.title: Probability that a face survives
pumac-2007-combinatorics-a-06.body:
There are $6\cdot1729=10374$ unit faces. The $9,10$ cubes expose $6(81+100)=1086$ faces, the $1,12$ cubes expose $6(1+144)=870$. Because cubes and orientations are random, any particular unit face is exposed with probability $\frac{1086}{10374}$ or $\frac{870}{10374}$ in a round, each with probability $\frac12$, independently over rounds. So it stays unpainted in a round with probability $1-\frac{1086+870}{2\cdot10374}=1-\frac{978}{10374}\approx0.905726$.

After $k$ rounds the expected painted fraction is $1-0.905726^k$: $k=6$: $0.4479$, $k=7$: $0.49999$, $k=8$: $0.5471$. The closest to one half is $k=7$.

**Answer: 7**

pumac-2007-combinatorics-a-07.title: Domination of the inner 5 x 5 board
pumac-2007-combinatorics-a-07.body:
White squares on the border of the table already touch the edge, so only the $25$ inner squares $(\text{rows }2\text{--}6,\ \text{columns }2\text{--}6)$ must be black or have a black neighbour. A black square dominates at most $5$ inner squares, so at least $5$ are needed; a black border square dominates only one inner square and can be replaced by its inner neighbour, so the question is the domination number of the $5\times5$ grid graph, which is $7$ (an exhaustive search shows $6$ black squares cannot work).

Seven suffice, e.g. (rows and columns $1$ to $7$; $\#$ = black)
$$\begin{array}{ccccccc}.&.&.&.&.&.&.\\.&\#&.&\#&.&.&.\\.&.&.&.&.&\#&.\\.&.&\#&.&.&.&.\\.&.&.&.&\#&.&.\\.&\#&.&.&\#&.&.\\.&.&.&.&.&.&.\end{array}$$

**Answer: 7**

pumac-2007-combinatorics-a-08.title: Signed count
pumac-2007-combinatorics-a-08.body:
Let $\varepsilon_i=+1$ if $a_ib_i$ is even and $-1$ if odd. The number of pairs with an even sum equals $\frac12\left(\text{total}+\sum\prod\varepsilon_i\right)$, and the sum of products factorises over positions.

Position $1$ (digits $1$ to $9$, since the number has exactly $2007$ digits): $81$ pairs, $25$ with both odd, $56$ even: contribution to the signed sum $56-25=31$. Positions $2,\dots,2007$ (digits $0$ to $9$): $100$ pairs, $25$ odd, $75$ even: $75-25=50$.

$$\#=\frac{81\cdot100^{2006}+31\cdot50^{2006}}2=4050\cdot100^{2005}+775\cdot50^{2005}.$$

(Check on $2$-digit numbers: $\frac{8100+1550}{2}=4825$, equal to a direct count.)

**Answer: $4050\cdot100^{2005}+775\cdot50^{2005}$**

pumac-2007-combinatorics-a-09.title: Choose the first block
pumac-2007-combinatorics-a-09.body:
A permutation with exactly one descent is two increasing runs: pick the set $S$ of values forming the first run (placed in increasing order) and the remaining values form the second run (increasing). Every subset $S$ gives a permutation, except that the identity arises from every initial segment $S=\{1,\dots,k\}$ ($k=0,\dots,2007$), and these give no descent. All other subsets give exactly one descent and distinct permutations. So the count is $2^{2007}-(2007+1)=2^{2007}-2008$.

**Answer: $2^{2007}-2008$**

pumac-2007-combinatorics-a-10.title: An arrangement of 37 and a row-by-row search
pumac-2007-combinatorics-a-10.body:
The first condition says the empty squares form an independent set (no two adjacent), so at least $32$ pawns are needed; the second condition forces extra adjacent pawn pairs in every row and column window. An exhaustive dynamic programme over the rows (state: the previous row and, for each column, whether an adjacent pair has already occurred in the first $7$ rows and in rows $2$ to $8$) gives the minimum $37$.

An arrangement with $37$ pawns ($P$ = pawn):
$$\begin{array}{cccccccc}.&P&P&.&P&.&P&.\\P&.&P&P&.&P&.&P\\.&P&P&.&P&.&P&.\\P&P&.&P&.&P&P&P\\P&.&P&.&P&P&.&P\\.&P&.&P&P&.&P&.\\P&.&P&P&.&P&.&P\\.&P&P&.&P&.&P&.\end{array}$$
No two empty squares are adjacent and every row and column window of $7$ contains two adjacent pawns (checked by computer).

**Answer: 37**
